Chapter 7: The Power of Education and Conscious Awakening
Change—it usually starts with a simple question: “Why?” For so many of us, the first steps toward real empowerment happen in the most unexpected places. Maybe it’s a classroom, a book club, or just a late-night chat with friends. See, education isn’t only about memorizing facts or acing tests. At its core, it’s about learning to see the world with fresh eyes.
I remember sitting in a lecture once, hearing about this idea called the “male gaze.” And suddenly, so much clicked into place. That uneasy feeling while watching certain movies, the pressure to look a certain way, or even just the sense of being watched—especially when you’re all by yourself. It’s like someone flipped on the lights in a dark room. The world itself hasn’t changed, but your view of it has.
For some, that sense of awakening comes through reading—finding writers who finally put words to feelings you’ve carried for years. Maybe things that always felt off, but you never quite knew how to say them out loud. Their words become a lifeline, helping you make sense of those isolating experiences. And there’s comfort in realizing you’re not the only one who’s felt this way, or asked these questions, or wondered how to push back.
But here’s something important—education isn’t always formal. Sometimes it’s just a friend calling out a casual sexist joke, or a post on social media that completely flips your perspective. Let’s be honest, those moments can be uncomfortable—even a little painful. It’s tough to admit the ways we’ve gone along with things that hurt us, or even the ways we might’ve hurt others. But that discomfort? That’s often where real growth begins.
Most of us don’t even realize how much we’ve soaked up without thinking. Conscious awakening isn’t a one-and-done deal—it’s this ongoing journey, made up of little shifts that slowly transform how we see everything. It’s about being willing to listen, to own up when you’re wrong, and to keep learning, even when it isn’t easy.
There’s this great story about a group of friends who start meeting once a month to talk about feminist books. At first, everyone’s a little nervous, tossing in disclaimers and laughing it off. But as time goes on, trust builds. People share stories they’ve never told anyone, ask questions they were scared to ask, and push each other to look at things more deeply. That group becomes their anchor—a reminder that you don’t have to figure everything out alone.
So, when you think about education, try seeing it as less about having the right answers, and more about staying curious. It’s about being open, searching for new perspectives, and not settling for the easy explanations. The more you learn, the more you realize just how much there is left to discover.
